verdict.summary: Strava prohibits using its API data in an AI application. This includes sending Strava data to an LLM context window. Do not connect Strava data to this AI agent.
verdict.activeEffort: 6–8 hours (sum of the step estimates below). Not applicable for this AI integration because Strava prohibits this use.
verdict.waitTime: Not applicable: do not submit this AI use for review.
verdict.mainGate: Strava prohibits using API materials or Strava data in the development, training, evaluation, or operation of any AI application.

recommendation.text: Do not connect Strava to this AI agent. Build a non-AI Strava feature instead, or obtain written permission before using any Strava data.

essentials.text: Access tokens expire after six hours. Store each replacement refresh token atomically, because the old token stops working.

sources.quote: Access tokens expire six hours after they are created
Once a new refresh token code has been returned, the older code will no longer work.
Applications should persist the refresh token contained in the response, and always use the most recent refresh token

essentials.text: Set an Authorization Callback Domain in API Settings. Production redirects must use a real domain under that configured domain.

sources.quote: When taking your app live, change “Authorization Callback Domain” to a real domain.
Must be within the callback domain specified by the application. localhost and 127.0.0.1 are white-listed.

essentials.text: New apps allow only your own account. You can self-upgrade to ten connected customers, but customer 11 requires review.

sources.quote: All new applications start in single-player mode. This is the default state where only your own Strava account can authenticate with the app
you can now self-upgrade to a new level of access (up to 10 athletes) in the Standard Tier directly from your API settings dashboard -- no formal review required.
If you want to scale beyond 10 connected athletes you’ll need to submit your app for review. Until your app has been reviewed, you won't be able to authenticate any additional athletes to your app.

essentials.text: The initial overall limit is 200 requests per 15 minutes and 2,000 daily. At ten customers, the overall limit is 400 requests per 15 minutes and 4,000 daily.

sources.quote: 200 requests every 15 minutes, with up to 2,000 requests per day.
Read read limits: 200 requests / 15min & 2,000 requests / day Overall rate limits: 400 requests / 15min & 4,000 requests / day

essentials.text: A Strava subscription is required before creating an app. Pricing varies by region and is shown on Strava's pricing page.

sources.quote: A Strava subscription is a prerequisite for creating an app.
Visit https://www.strava.com/pricing to see the subscription price in your region.

essentials.text: Use one registered OAuth 2.0 app. Keep its client secret on your server, and never send Strava data through AI tooling.

sources.quote: Strava uses OAuth2 for authentication to the V3 API.
The secret is used for authentication and should never be shared.
You may not use the Strava API Materials or Strava Data, directly or indirectly, in connection with the development, training, evaluation, or operation of any AI Application.

essentials.text: Review applies when adding customer 11 or more. Submit the Developer Program form with screenshots of every Strava-data screen and the Connect with Strava button.

sources.quote: Please complete our Developer Program form for review and be sure to include screenshots of all the places Strava data is shown and the "Connect with Strava" button in your application.
Strava does not commit to a fixed review-time service-level agreement

essentials.text: Validate OAuth state against the login session. For webhooks, validate the challenge and return HTTP 200 within two seconds.

sources.quote: The state parameter will be always included in the response if it was initially provided by the application.
An identical string will be included in the validation request made by Strava's subscription service.
The subscription callback endpoint must acknowledge the POST of each new event with a status code of 200 OK within two seconds.

requests.text: Redirect the user here and verify the returned state and granted scopes.

sources.quote: Redirect the user to GET https://www.strava.com/oauth/authorize .

scope 
 required string, in query
 Requested scopes, as a comma- or URL-safe space-delimited string, e.g. "activity:read_all,activity:write" or "activity:read_all%20activity:write".

requests.label: Send the user to sign in

requests.text: Exchange the short-lived, single-use authorization code for access and refresh tokens.

sources.quote:
curl -X POST https://www.strava.com/api/v3/oauth/token \
 -d client_id=ReplaceWithClientID \
 -d client_secret=ReplaceWithClientSecret \
 -d code=ReplaceWithCode \
 -d grant_type=authorization_code
code is short lived and can only be used once.

requests.label: Exchange the code for tokens
requests.curl:
curl -X POST https://www.strava.com/api/v3/oauth/token \
  -d client_id=YOUR_CLIENT_ID \
  -d client_secret=YOUR_CLIENT_SECRET \
  -d code=AUTH_CODE \
  -d grant_type=authorization_code

requests.text: Store the refresh token returned by this response because the prior one may be invalidated.

sources.quote:
curl -X POST https://www.strava.com/api/v3/oauth/token \
 -d client_id=ReplaceWithClientID \
 -d client_secret=ReplaceWithClientSecret \
 -d grant_type=refresh_token \
 -d refresh_token=ReplaceWithRefreshToken
Once a new refresh token is returned, the older refresh token is invalidated immediately.

requests.label: Refresh the access token
requests.curl:
curl -X POST https://www.strava.com/api/v3/oauth/token \
  -d client_id=YOUR_CLIENT_ID \
  -d client_secret=YOUR_CLIENT_SECRET \
  -d grant_type=refresh_token \
  -d refresh_token=REFRESH_TOKEN

requests.text: Retrieve the authenticated athlete profile to confirm the connection.

sources.quote: curl -G https://www.strava.com/api/v3/athlete -H "Authorization: Bearer ReplaceWithAccessToken"

requests.label: Check the connection

requests.text: Revoke the token and all associated tokens using HTTP Basic authentication.

sources.quote: As of June 1, 2026 applications can choose to leverage the endpoint POST https://www.strava.com/oauth/revoke .
Authenticate using HTTP Basic Auth with your application's client_id and client_secret: Authorization: Basic

curl -X POST "https://www.strava.com/oauth/revoke" \
 -H "Authorization: Basic <base64(client_id:client_secret)>" \
 -H "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" \
 -d "token=<access_or_refresh_token>"

requests.label: Revoke access
